summary: Edge HTTP/3 idempotency token fragmentation causing duplicate tool invocations from TS streaming clients
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using the TS streaming SDK over HTTP/3 through our edge network are observing duplicate external tool/webhook invocations when a request is retried. The duplicates correlate with very long idempotency tokens (generated by the customer) that exceed typical header frame sizes and appear to be fragmented across QUIC frames. Edge proxies sometimes normalize reassembled headers differently on retry paths, leading to the server treating retried requests as new (no idempotency match).

Impact:
- OmniPay reports duplicate payment-notification webhook posts from their orchestration service; duplicates observed ~1-3% of streaming retries in eu-west.
- Potential revenue/customer trust impact; duplicates trigger downstream compensating transactions.

Environment:
- Hosted Redwood API (edge-enabled HTTP/3), prod, eu-west
- TS SDK v1.9.2 with streaming resume/reconnect enabled
- Customer uses long base64-encoded idempotency keys (~420 chars) generated by their orchestration layer

Observed behavior:
- Client sends stream, connection interruption causes SDK reconnect with resume token and retry.
- Edge receives retry but QUIC frame fragmentation causes the idempotency header to be split; after internal reassembly the header string differs (insertion of padding or percent-decoding in path through sidecar).
- Serving runtime does not match previous idempotency record; tool/function calls (webhook posts) are executed again.

Expected behavior:
- Retries that include the same idempotency key should be deduplicated and not cause re-execution of external tool calls when the original attempt succeeded or was in-flight.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use TS SDK v1.9.2 streaming client pointed at api.redwood.ai over HTTP/3.
2) Provide a long base64 idempotency key (> 380 chars) in x-redwood-idempotency header.
3) Begin a streaming request that triggers a tool/function call (webhook) mid-stream.
4) Simulate a connection interruption (network drop) and allow the SDK to reconnect/resume.
5) Observe webhook endpoint receiving duplicate POSTs for same logical action.

Notes: reproduces reliably when client and edge sidecar MTU/fragment behavior forces header to be split across QUIC frames. Short keys (< 120 chars) do not reproduce.
logs:
- edge-proxy trace: edge-trace=et-20260310-7b4a; request_id=rq-8f3c; header-length=428
- serving-runtime: TRACE:rq-8f3c idempotency_lookup miss (normalized_key=z2F... vs original z2F... padding mismatch)
- webhook logs (customer): webhook_id=wh-1122 timestamp=2026-03-10T15:22:33Z status=200; webhook_id=wh-1122 timestamp=2026-03-10T15:22:41Z status=200 (duplicate)
- pcap attached to internal S3: s3://redwood-internal/pcaps/SUP-975310/quic-frag-2026-03-10.pcap
- Related edge proxy log snippet: "POST /v1/stream 200 idempotency: received-length=428 reassembled-length=430 norm-key=..."
investigation:
Initial triage (Support): confirmed duplicates only when idempotency header length > ~360 chars and when HTTP/3 path used. Customer reproduced with network simulation.
SRE/Edge team checked edge-proxy code path: we discovered an intermediate sidecar (third-party L7) performing percent-decoding of header fragments when reassembling QUIC frames; that decoder will sometimes insert '=' padding characters when fragments align differently on retry. This produces a different canonical idempotency token string.
TS SDK team confirmed that v1.9.2 will automatically attempt resume with the same header value but will resend headers in a new packet set; edge reassembly path difference explains divergence.
We correlated request ids and webhook timestamps; serving runtime records show idempotency store entries keyed by normalized string, so token mismatch leads to new execution.
Interim workaround tested: customer changed idempotency key generation to a short hex digest (64 chars) and duplicates stopped.
Further findings: PR proposed to edge-proxy to canonicalize header values before forwarding (github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/489). A smaller SDK patch to add client-side canonicalization/trim policy is in review (github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/1220).
resolution:
Workaround implemented for customer: advise customers to use <=128 char canonical idempotency keys (hex or SHA256 truncated) until a permanent fix is rolled out. OmniPay applied the temporary change and verified zero duplicates for 48 hours.
Planned permanent fixes:
- Short-term (~72h): edge-proxy hotfix to normalize base64 headers during QUIC reassembly (PR #489 under review).
- Medium-term: TS SDK change to apply a canonicalization and max-length warning at key creation time; publish docs guidance (PR #1220).
- Long-term: add server-side tolerant idempotency matching (hash and canonical fallback) to avoid strict string equality.
Follow-ups: monitor eu-west metrics and roll edge-proxy fix to other regions after validation.
Status: in progress; ETA for edge hotfix 2026-03-14, SDK release v1.9.3 ETA 2026-03-16.
